name: The Kerberos Double-Hop Problem & Fixes
description: When you PSRemote/WinRS into host A, your credentials are NOT forwarded to a second hop (host B / the DC) - so tools run in that remote session fail to authenticate onward ('Access Denied' reaching the DC from A). This is the #1 CRTP exam gotcha. Fix it by giving the session an actual ticket (createnetonly + PTT / OverPass-the-Hash) instead of relying on delegation, or use CredSSP.

steps.label: Recognise it: from a remote session, DC access fails
steps.command: Invoke-Command -ComputerName <hostA> -ScriptBlock { Get-Domain }   # works local to A but Get-DomainUser against the DC -> Access Denied (no creds on 2nd hop)

steps.label: Fix (preferred): spawn a clean logon session
Inject a TGT into that new session (no 2nd hop needed)
Now tools in that window reach the DC directly
steps.command: Get-DomainUser -Domain <domain>   # ticket is present in this logon session

examples.label: OverPass-the-Hash to avoid the double hop entirely
CredSSP (official fix, but sends plaintext creds to host A)

recommended.note: Overpass-the-Hash gives the session a real ticket
The lateral-movement channel that triggers the double-hop
Dump creds once you can reach the target

notes: WHY it happens: interactive PSRemoting authenticates you to host A with Kerberos, but host A has no way to prove your identity to host B unless delegation is configured - your TGT never lands on A. FIXES: (1) createnetonly spawns a process with a blank NEW logon session, then Rubeus asktgt /ptt injects a TGT into it - all onward auth uses that ticket, no delegation needed (cleanest for the exam). (2) OverPass-the-Hash / Pass-the-Ticket locally, then run tools from that shell. (3) CredSSP (Enable-WSManCredSSP -Role Client -DelegateComputer <A> on your box; -Role Server on A) - simplest but sends plaintext creds to A and is loud. (4) Unconstrained/constrained delegation if the account has it. Prefer AES (/aes256) over /rc4 for ticket ops.

references.title: harmj0y - PowerShell Remoting & the Double Hop

defense.why_it_works: Kerberos does not forward a user's TGT to a service they authenticate to (by design). In a PowerShell Remoting session on host A, the logon is a network logon (type 3) with no delegatable credential, so any onward authentication from A to a third host (B/DC) has no ticket to present and fails. Attackers work around this by placing an actual usable ticket into a logon session: Rubeus createnetonly creates a sacrificial logon session (LOGON32_LOGON_NEW_CREDENTIALS) and asktgt /ptt injects a TGT into it, so onward Kerberos auth succeeds without any delegation being configured. CredSSP works instead by delegating the plaintext credential to host A.
defense.prerequisites: A foothold that requires reaching a second hop (remote PSSession/WinRS on host A, then targeting the DC or host B). For the createnetonly fix: the user's NT hash or AES key (from prior dumping). For CredSSP: ability to enable CredSSP client-side and the server allowing it.
defense.impact: T1550.003 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Ticket + T1021.006 WinRM. Enables full onward lateral movement (A -> DC) that would otherwise fail, so it is a key enabler of the whole CRTP kill chain rather than a standalone escalation.
defense.detection: Event 4624 Type 9 (NewCredentials logon) from createnetonly - an unusual logon type on a workstation is a strong signal. Rubeus createnetonly + asktgt leaves a TGT request (4768) with an RC4 or mismatched-from-context ticket. CredSSP: plaintext credential delegation and Event 4624 Type 3 followed by onward auth. MDI flags ticket anomalies (RC4 TGTs, tickets without prior AS-REQ).
defense.artifacts: Event 4624 Logon Type 9 (seclogo / NewCredentials) | Event 4768 TGT request from a process like powershell.exe shortly after a createnetonly-spawned process | CredSSP: WSMan CredSSP policy change (Enable-WSManCredSSP) in registry HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\CredentialsDelegation
defense.prevention:
Apply the tiering model so admins never authenticate to lower-tier hosts (removes the need for and risk of double-hop). Avoid enabling CredSSP (it exposes plaintext creds on the target). Use Protected Users group (blocks NTLM/RC4 and credential delegation for members). Monitor Logon Type 9 events. Deploy MDI for Kerberos anomaly detection.
Credential Access Protection: keep privileged tickets/keys off lower-tier hosts.
Privileged Account Management: DAs log on only to Tier-0 systems.
defense.evasion: Use /aes256 instead of /rc4 for the injected TGT to avoid RC4-downgrade detections. Keep the sacrificial process short-lived. Prefer createnetonly+PTT over CredSSP (no plaintext credential hits the target).
defense.misconfiguration: Unconstrained or overly-broad constrained delegation configured on service accounts (lets the double-hop succeed trivially and is separately abusable). CredSSP enabled domain-wide. Admins authenticating interactively to workstations.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# CredSSP enabled on clients (allows plaintext credential delegation):
Get-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\Auth\CredSSP
# Value True -> credentials delegated in plaintext to the remote host

# Account is NOT in Protected Users, uses RC4, and has delegation -> double-hop trivially works
defense.secure_config:
# Do not enable CredSSP unless required; if enabled, scope DelegateComputer tightly.
# Add privileged accounts to Protected Users (blocks delegation + RC4):
Add-ADGroupMember -Identity 'Protected Users' -Members <admin>

# Enforce tiering: deny DA interactive/remote logon to non-Tier-0:
# GPO -> Deny log on through Remote Desktop / Deny access to this computer from the network for Tier-0 accounts on lower tiers

# Alert on Logon Type 9:
# EventID=4624 AND LogonType=9 AND LogonProcessName='seclogo' -> review
